subject: history_social
passage: Setting out from his hometown of Tangier, in Morocco, in 1325 at the age of twenty-one, ______ That pilgrimage turned out to be only the first stage of his travels, which eventually carried him as far as India and China. He did not settle back in Morocco for about twenty-four years.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: Ibn Battuta's first journey took him across North Africa to Mecca.
choices.B: a journey across North Africa to Mecca was begun by Ibn Battuta.
choices.C: Ibn Battuta traveled across North Africa on his way to Mecca.
choices.D: North Africa was crossed by Ibn Battuta on his way to Mecca.

explanation.why: The introductory phrase "Setting out from his hometown of Tangier ... at the age of twenty-one" describes a person. The subject right after the comma must be that person, Ibn Battuta.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The subject is "Ibn Battuta's first journey," so the sentence says the journey was twenty-one and set out from its hometown.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The subject is "a journey," so the phrase wrongly describes the journey as setting out from its hometown at twenty-one.
explanation.C: Correct. "Ibn Battuta" comes right after the introductory phrase, so he is the one setting out from Tangier at twenty-one.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The subject is "North Africa," so the sentence says North Africa set out from Tangier.
